Definition: from a primary ἔχθω (to hate); hateful (passively, odious, or actively, hostile); usually as a noun, an adversary (especially Satan):--enemy, foe.
BiblicalUsage: An enemy is one who hates and opposes, and the Bible names enemies both human and spiritual, with Satan at the head of them. Jesus commands us to love our enemies and pray for those who persecute us, Zechariah's song promises deliverance from the hand of our enemies, and Paul says we were reconciled to God while we were still enemies. The last enemy, Paul says, is death itself, and it will be destroyed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe loving enemies is the hardest command Jesus gave, and the clearest proof of His life in us. God loved me while I was His enemy, so I have no excuse for hating mine.
